title: Source-open restriction of exceptional scalar mates
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On either the ordinary etale or pro-etale site let $\mathcal C_{T,R}=D^b_{ctf}(T,R)$ mean the full category of constant-$R$ module complexes with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude: tensor with any degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer]. Write $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The finite Tate line is $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ on the etale site and its comparison inverse image on the pro-etale site; $(d)$ denotes tensor with its $d$th tensor power [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist].
Let $f:X\to Y$ be any separated finite-type morphism and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion; put $g=fj$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Choose compactifications with standing middle schemes [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On pro-etale finite-Tor categories use $F_{h,R}=Rh_{!,R}\dashv G_{h,R}=h_R^!$ for $h=f,g$, $R=A,B$ [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation], and $J_R=Dj_{!,R}\dashv U_R=j_R^*$ with counit $v_R$ [det-sf-mate-open-restriction]. Identify $F_{g,R}$ with $F_{f,R}J_R$ and $G_{g,R}$ with $U_RG_{f,R}$ by the canonical adjunction-preserving composition and refinement comparisons [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Let $b_h:T_YF_{h,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{h,B}T_{\mathrm{source}(h)}$ be the proper-counit/open-tensor comparison [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. Define $c_h:T_{\mathrm{source}(h)}G_{h,A}\to G_{h,B}T_Y$ as the unique counit transpose satisfying
$$\epsilon_{h,B}\circ F_{h,B}(c_h)=T_Y(\epsilon_{h,A})\circ b_h(G_{h,A}-)^{-1}.$$
Let $a_j:T_UU_A\xrightarrow{\sim}U_BT_X$ be the canonical scalar/restriction comparison [def-sp-constant-scalar-pullback-comparison]. For every $K\in\mathcal C_{Y,A}$ one has, under the stated right-adjoint comparisons,
$$c_{g,K}=U_B(c_{f,K})\circ a_j(G_{f,A}K).$$
Equivalently $j^*c_f$ is $c_g$ under the canonical tensor/restriction identification. This is equality of the specified derived morphisms, for an arbitrary $f$; no smoothness or invertibility of $c_f,c_g$ is assumed.

proof.text:
Fix $K$ and put $M=G_{f,A}K$ and $L=U_AM$. Use the adjunction-preserving composition identifications in the statement throughout; thus $F_{g,R}=F_{f,R}J_R$, $G_{g,R}=U_RG_{f,R}$. The composite-adjunction definition gives
$$\epsilon_{g,R,K}=\epsilon_{f,R,K}\circ F_{f,R}(v_{R,G_{f,R}K}).$$
The coefficient/composition square of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], applied to $U\xrightarrow{j}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$, gives, in these identifications,
$$b_g(L)=F_{f,B}(b_j(L))\circ b_f(J_AL).$$
Here $b_j:T_XJ_A\simeq J_BT_U$ is the normalized open tensor map. The refinement clause of that same node ensures this formula for the chosen compactifications, including comparison through a common refinement. All inputs are in the finite-Tor categories stipulated in the statement. That node states the pro-etale composition square for etale-origin objects; by [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] (the schemes are qcqs and $A,B$ are finite, hence Noetherian) $\nu_U^*$ is an equivalence $D^b_{ctf}(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)\simeq\mathcal C_{U,A}$, so $L\simeq\nu_U^*L'$ with $L'$ etale bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude, and naturality of both sides of the square in $L$ transfers it to $L$. The site/composition identifications are thus the specified etale-origin ones of that node and the adjunction transfer, not arbitrary isomorphisms of the underlying functors.

source.place: Locality paragraph: source-open restriction and composition of counit transposes; explicit cancellation argument

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sp-open-proetale-counit-scalar] to $M$. Its identity for the actual open counit is
$$v_{B,T_XM}\circ J_B(a_{j,M})\circ b_j(L)=T_X(v_{A,M}).$$
Since $b_j(L)$ is invertible, right-composition with its inverse gives the precisely typed equality
$$v_{B,T_XM}\circ J_B(a_{j,M})=T_X(v_{A,M})\circ b_j(L)^{-1}.$$
Both sides go from $J_BT_UL$ to $T_XM$. This uses no inverse of an exceptional comparison.

source.place: Locality paragraph: source-open restriction and composition of counit transposes; explicit cancellation argument

proof.text:
Set $d_K=U_B(c_{f,K})\circ a_{j,M}:T_UL\to U_BG_{f,B}T_YK$ and take its counit transpose
$$\tau=\epsilon_{g,B,T_YK}\circ F_{f,B}J_B(d_K).$$
Naturality of $v_B:J_BU_B\to1$, evaluated at $c_{f,K}:T_XM\to G_{f,B}T_YK$, says
$$v_{B,G_{f,B}T_YK}\circ J_BU_B(c_{f,K})=c_{f,K}\circ v_{B,T_XM}.$$
Insert the composite counit from step 1, then this equality, and then step 2. The defining counit equation for $c_f$ in the statement yields
$$\begin{aligned}
\tau&=\epsilon_{f,B,T_YK}\circ F_{f,B}(c_{f,K})\circ F_{f,B}\bigl(v_{B,T_XM}\circ J_B(a_{j,M})\bigr)\\
&=T_Y(\epsilon_{f,A,K})\circ b_f(M)^{-1}\circ F_{f,B}(T_X(v_{A,M}))\circ F_{f,B}(b_j(L)^{-1}).
\end{aligned}$$
This is just naturality, functoriality and substitution of the displayed identities.

source.place: Locality paragraph: source-open restriction and composition of counit transposes; explicit cancellation argument

proof.text:
The comparison $b_f$ is natural by [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. Apply its naturality square to $v_{A,M}:J_AL\to M$ and compose with inverses of its two isomorphism components. This gives
$$b_f(M)^{-1}\circ F_{f,B}(T_X(v_{A,M}))=T_Y(F_{f,A}(v_{A,M}))\circ b_f(J_AL)^{-1}.$$
Substitute in step 3. Functoriality of $T_Y$, the composite-counit equation in step 1, and inversion of the two-factor expression for $b_g(L)$ in step 1 give
$$\begin{aligned}
\tau&=T_Y\bigl(\epsilon_{f,A,K}\circ F_{f,A}(v_{A,M})\bigr)\circ b_f(J_AL)^{-1}\circ F_{f,B}(b_j(L)^{-1})\\
&=T_Y(\epsilon_{g,A,K})\circ b_g(L)^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The order of the inverse factors is reversed, so their composite has source $F_{g,B}T_UL$ and target $T_YF_{g,A}L$.

source.place: Locality paragraph: source-open restriction and composition of counit transposes; explicit cancellation argument

proof.text: By definition in the statement, $c_{g,K}$ has counit transpose $T_Y(\epsilon_{g,A,K})\circ b_g(G_{g,A}K)^{-1}$; here $G_{g,A}K=L$. Step 4 proves that $d_K$ has this very transpose. The composite adjunction's Hom bijection in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] is a bijection, hence injective. Therefore $d_K=c_{g,K}$, which is the required equality for each $K$. No assertion about smoothness, a chart, or invertibility of either right mate enters this argument.

I recomputed each one with types: the composite counit eps_f F_f(v); b_g(L) = F_f(b_j(L)) b_f(J_A L) from the (j,f) composition clause of lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility; the open-counit equation of lem-sp-open-proetale-counit-scalar with right-composition by b_j^{-1}; naturality of v at c_f and of b_f at v_{A,M}, with the inverse order correct; and injectivity of the composite Hom bijection.
